# Azure Authentication Demo

This runbook demonstrates the `<AzureAuth>` block. It signs in with the Azure CLI (`az login`), a device code, or a service principal, and keeps each block's sign-in in its own `AZURE_CONFIG_DIR`, so the blocks here don't collide with each other or change your own `~/.azure`.

---

## 1. Basic usage

With no `detectCredentials` prop, the block looks for a service principal in `ARM_*` / `AZURE_*` environment variables, then for your existing `az login`, and asks you to confirm before using it. After signing in it asks you to pick a tenant and subscription, unless there's only one of each.

```mdx
<AzureAuth id="azure-auth" title="Sign in to Azure" />
```

<AzureAuth
  id="azure-auth"
  title="Sign in to Azure"
  description="Sign in with the method you prefer. The sign-in is used by the steps below."
/>

<Command
  id="show-account"
  path="scripts/show-account.sh"
  title="Show the signed-in account"
  description="Runs `az account show` with this block's sign-in, and prints the variables AzureAuth set."
  azureAuthId="azure-auth"
  successMessage="Signed in to Azure."
/>

<Check
  id="check-azure-env"
  path="checks/verify-azure-env.sh"
  title="Check the Azure environment variables"
  description="Checks the variables `azurerm` and the Azure SDKs read are consistent. Doesn't call Azure."
  azureAuthId="azure-auth"
  successMessage="The Azure variables are consistent."
  failMessage="The Azure variables are missing or inconsistent."
/>

---

## 2. Pinning a tenant and subscription

`tenantId` and `subscriptionId` skip the picker. A tenant ID also sends interactive sign-in straight to that tenant, which is how a guest signs in to another organization's tenant. Both take template expressions.

<Inputs id="azure-target">
```yaml
variables:
  - name: TenantId
    type: string
    description: The tenant to sign in to (ID or domain)
    default: ""
```
</Inputs>

```mdx
<AzureAuth
  id="azure-pinned"
  tenantId="{{ .inputs.TenantId }}"
  inputsId="azure-target"
  defaultTab="device_code"
/>
```

<AzureAuth
  id="azure-pinned"
  title="Sign in to a specific tenant"
  tenantId="{{ .inputs.TenantId }}"
  inputsId="azure-target"
  defaultTab="device_code"
  detectCredentials={false}
/>

<Command
  id="show-pinned-account"
  path="scripts/show-account.sh"
  title="Show the pinned sign-in"
  azureAuthId="azure-pinned"
/>

---

## 3. Requiring roles

`requiredRoles` checks the principal's role assignments after sign-in, and fails the sign-in with the roles that are missing. A landing-zone bootstrap, for example, needs User Access Administrator at the root scope.

```mdx
<AzureAuth
  id="azure-admin"
  requiredRoles={[
    { role: "User Access Administrator", scope: "/" },
    { role: "Owner", scope: "subscription" },
  ]}
/>
```

<AzureAuth
  id="azure-admin"
  title="Sign in as a landing-zone administrator"
  detectCredentials={['cli']}
  requiredRoles={[
    { role: "User Access Administrator", scope: "/" },
    { role: "Owner", scope: "subscription" },
  ]}
/>

---

## 4. Service principal from the environment

Detection with a prefix reads `CI_ARM_CLIENT_ID`, `CI_ARM_TENANT_ID` and `CI_ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` (or the `AZURE_*` names).

```mdx
<AzureAuth id="azure-ci" detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: 'CI_' } }]} defaultTab="service_principal" />
```

<AzureAuth
  id="azure-ci"
  title="Sign in as a CI service principal"
  detectCredentials={[{ env: { prefix: 'CI_' } }]}
  defaultTab="service_principal"
/>
